answer: Nectar-Weighted Vertex Auctions. Each agent submits a vertex in a coordination graph; its influence equals nectar, a resource minted only by completing verified cross-agent tasks and decaying per epoch. Proposals touching k distinct vertices pay basalt: a fee that scales superlinearly in k and is redistributed to the touched vertices. Sybils must split influence across many low-nectar vertices, so each extra identity multiplies basalt cost while contributing negligible nectar, making coordinated capture economically dominated by honest single-vertex participation.
